system.name: Altair
system.description: One of the vertices of the Summer Triangle, Altair is an A7V star just 16.7 light-years away. It spins so rapidly — once every 9 hours — that it is noticeably flattened at the poles, bulging at its equator.

altair.name: Altair
altair.description: An A7V white star and one of the fastest-rotating stars known, completing a full rotation in just under 9 hours. Its equator is flung outward by centrifugal force, making Altair about 20% wider at the equator than at the poles — a shape confirmed by interferometric imaging.
altair.funFact: In 2006, Altair became one of the first stars ever to be directly imaged in sufficient resolution to reveal its disc shape — showing the bulging equator predicted by its rapid spin.
